assets.description:
Shared World combat Sun Glare Standard is a procedural-runtime-effect added by the final Zaylins gameplay, sensory, environmental, interaction, customization, and cohesion sweep for shared-world. It closes the “combat runtime-vfx” gap with a named production asset rather than an invisible placeholder, a recycled generic puff, an unrelated object, or a crude primitive approximation. The result must communicate its purpose immediately through silhouette, motion, timing, optical response, state, surface contact, or interaction while following cross-town physical realism, controlled stylization, legible silhouettes, accessibility, and consistent gameplay language.

Required production anatomy: named emitter origin, primary particle or optical layer, secondary breakup layer, timing envelope, surface or volume response, quality tiers, pooling and cleanup rule, reduced-motion and reduced-flash alternative. Every component is functional. Components connect through believable supports, timing relationships, strand roots, anatomy, attachment points, projection rules, emitter origins, service paths, collision-safe boundaries, or state transitions appropriate to Shared World combat Sun Glare Standard. Materials and response layers include particle sprite or procedural field, optical or emissive layer, surface-response mask, accessibility fallback. Separation follows real construction, biological growth, light transport, contamination, weather, particle behavior, hair-fiber behavior, or gameplay state rather than arbitrary color blocks.

Implementation defines a stable named origin, deterministic forward or projection direction, scale envelope, spawn or placement conditions, looping or one-shot lifecycle, transition timing, cleanup and pooling, network relevance, quality tiers, editor-preview metadata, and validation thresholds. Dependencies on surfaces, bodies, vehicles, weapons, water, wind, camera, lighting, audio, quests, or interaction sockets are explicit and testable. Close-range presentation needs convincing breakup, thickness, depth, hardware, strand structure, species anatomy, or layered motion. Distant presentation preserves the primary read without excessive triangles, overdraw, alpha sorting, particle count, shadows, or replication traffic.

Accessibility is mandatory. The asset does not rely on color alone. Flashing, injury feedback, camera motion, particle density, and hazard communication include reduced-flash, reduced-motion, reduced-particle, high-contrast, or icon alternatives where relevant. Injury effects default to non-graphic presentation. Stylized blood is abstract and optional, contains no gore or exposed anatomy, and has paint, spark, dust, and comic-impact alternatives. Hair uses a scalp-conforming root field, purposeful hairline, believable density and gravity, style-specific structure, silhouette variation, ear and nape clearance, recolor support, and secondary-motion planning. Afros are not bunched spheres. Locs are not identical cylinders. Braids and twists show interwoven rhythm, parting, tension, taper, and purposeful styling.

This specification never authorizes crude geometry. Every layer reinforces Shared World combat Sun Glare Standard, integrates with adjacent Zaylins systems, and passes recognition, lifecycle, town-style, accessibility, performance, and state review. Specialized GLBs remain outside the generic primitive Blender lane until a dedicated builder can satisfy this contract.

It closes the “combat connector” gap with a named production asset rather than an invisible placeholder, a recycled generic puff, an unrelated object, or a crude primitive approximation. The result must communicate its purpose immediately through silhouette, motion, timing, optical response, state, surface contact, or interaction while following cross-town physical realism, controlled stylization, legible silhouettes, accessibility, and consistent gameplay language.

Required production anatomy: primary structural span, start connection socket, end connection socket, load-bearing frame, service access, seal or transition trim, collision-safe boundary, LOD-preserved silhouette. Every component is functional. Components connect through believable supports, timing relationships, strand roots, anatomy, attachment points, projection rules, emitter origins, service paths, collision-safe boundaries, or state transitions appropriate to Shared World combat Transit Tube Straight Standard. Materials and response layers include structural material, connection hardware, seal or trim material, town-specific surface finish. Separation follows real construction, biological growth, light transport, contamination, weather, particle behavior, hair-fiber behavior, or gameplay state rather than arbitrary color blocks.

Implementation defines a stable named origin, deterministic forward or projection direction, scale envelope, spawn or placement conditions, looping or one-shot lifecycle, transition timing, cleanup and pooling, network relevance, quality tiers, editor-preview metadata, and validation thresholds. Dependencies on surfaces, bodies, vehicles, weapons, water, wind, camera, lighting, audio, quests, or interaction sockets are explicit and testable. Close-range presentation needs convincing breakup, thickness, depth, hardware, strand structure, species anatomy, or layered motion. Distant presentation preserves the primary read without excessive triangles, overdraw, alpha sorting, particle count, shadows, or replication traffic.

Accessibility is mandatory. The asset does not rely on color alone. Flashing, injury feedback, camera motion, particle density, and hazard communication include reduced-flash, reduced-motion, reduced-particle, high-contrast, or icon alternatives where relevant. Injury effects default to non-graphic presentation. Stylized blood is abstract and optional, contains no gore or exposed anatomy, and has paint, spark, dust, and comic-impact alternatives. This specification never authorizes crude geometry. Every layer reinforces Shared World combat Transit Tube Straight Standard, integrates with adjacent Zaylins systems, and passes recognition, lifecycle, town-style, accessibility, performance, and state review. Materials and response layers include base structural material, state-specific material, hardware or damage layer, indicator material. assets.description:
Shared World crowds Airlock Sealed Standard is a state-aware-model-builder added by the final Zaylins gameplay, sensory, environmental, interaction, customization, and cohesion sweep for shared-world. It closes the “crowds state-variant” gap with a named production asset rather than an invisible placeholder, a recycled generic puff, an unrelated object, or a crude primitive approximation. The result must communicate its purpose immediately through silhouette, motion, timing, optical response, state, surface contact, or interaction while following cross-town physical realism, controlled stylization, legible silhouettes, accessibility, and consistent gameplay language.

Required production anatomy: base object relationship, state-defining geometry, state-defining material layer, animation transition socket, collision state, interaction state, damage or repair metadata, LOD and swap policy. Every component is functional. Components connect through believable supports, timing relationships, strand roots, anatomy, attachment points, projection rules, emitter origins, service paths, collision-safe boundaries, or state transitions appropriate to Shared World crowds Airlock Sealed Standard. Materials and response layers include base structural material, state-specific material, hardware or damage layer, indicator material. Separation follows real construction, biological growth, light transport, contamination, weather, particle behavior, hair-fiber behavior, or gameplay state rather than arbitrary color blocks.

Implementation defines a stable named origin, deterministic forward or projection direction, scale envelope, spawn or placement conditions, looping or one-shot lifecycle, transition timing, cleanup and pooling, network relevance, quality tiers, editor-preview metadata, and validation thresholds. Dependencies on surfaces, bodies, vehicles, weapons, water, wind, camera, lighting, audio, quests, or interaction sockets are explicit and testable. Close-range presentation needs convincing breakup, thickness, depth, hardware, strand structure, species anatomy, or layered motion. Distant presentation preserves the primary read without excessive triangles, overdraw, alpha sorting, particle count, shadows, or replication traffic.

Accessibility is mandatory. The asset does not rely on color alone. Flashing, injury feedback, camera motion, particle density, and hazard communication include reduced-flash, reduced-motion, reduced-particle, high-contrast, or icon alternatives where relevant. Injury effects default to non-graphic presentation. Stylized blood is abstract and optional, contains no gore or exposed anatomy, and has paint, spark, dust, and comic-impact alternatives. Hair uses a scalp-conforming root field, purposeful hairline, believable density and gravity, style-specific structure, silhouette variation, ear and nape clearance, recolor support, and secondary-motion planning. Afros are not bunched spheres. Locs are not identical cylinders. Braids and twists show interwoven rhythm, parting, tension, taper, and purposeful styling.

This specification never authorizes crude geometry. Every layer reinforces Shared World crowds Airlock Sealed Standard, integrates with adjacent Zaylins systems, and passes recognition, lifecycle, town-style, accessibility, performance, and state review. Specialized GLBs remain outside the generic primitive Blender lane until a dedicated builder can satisfy this contract.

materialPlan.flexibleRule: Fabric, upholstery, leather, rubber, and flexible polymers require thickness, seams, compression or tension cues, stitching where visible, and roughness variation tied to handling.

assets.description:
Shared World crowds Chest Closed Standard is a state-aware-model-builder added by the final Zaylins gameplay, sensory, environmental, interaction, customization, and cohesion sweep for shared-world. It closes the “crowds state-variant” gap with a named production asset rather than an invisible placeholder, a recycled generic puff, an unrelated object, or a crude primitive approximation. The result must communicate its purpose immediately through silhouette, motion, timing, optical response, state, surface contact, or interaction while following cross-town physical realism, controlled stylization, legible silhouettes, accessibility, and consistent gameplay language.

Required production anatomy: base object relationship, state-defining geometry, state-defining material layer, animation transition socket, collision state, interaction state, damage or repair metadata, LOD and swap policy. Every component is functional. Components connect through believable supports, timing relationships, strand roots, anatomy, attachment points, projection rules, emitter origins, service paths, collision-safe boundaries, or state transitions appropriate to Shared World crowds Chest Closed Standard. Materials and response layers include base structural material, state-specific material, hardware or damage layer, indicator material. Separation follows real construction, biological growth, light transport, contamination, weather, particle behavior, hair-fiber behavior, or gameplay state rather than arbitrary color blocks.

Implementation defines a stable named origin, deterministic forward or projection direction, scale envelope, spawn or placement conditions, looping or one-shot lifecycle, transition timing, cleanup and pooling, network relevance, quality tiers, editor-preview metadata, and validation thresholds. Dependencies on surfaces, bodies, vehicles, weapons, water, wind, camera, lighting, audio, quests, or interaction sockets are explicit and testable. Close-range presentation needs convincing breakup, thickness, depth, hardware, strand structure, species anatomy, or layered motion. Distant presentation preserves the primary read without excessive triangles, overdraw, alpha sorting, particle count, shadows, or replication traffic.

Accessibility is mandatory. The asset does not rely on color alone. Flashing, injury feedback, camera motion, particle density, and hazard communication include reduced-flash, reduced-motion, reduced-particle, high-contrast, or icon alternatives where relevant. Injury effects default to non-graphic presentation. Stylized blood is abstract and optional, contains no gore or exposed anatomy, and has paint, spark, dust, and comic-impact alternatives. Hair uses a scalp-conforming root field, purposeful hairline, believable density and gravity, style-specific structure, silhouette variation, ear and nape clearance, recolor support, and secondary-motion planning. Afros are not bunched spheres. Locs are not identical cylinders. Braids and twists show interwoven rhythm, parting, tension, taper, and purposeful styling.

This specification never authorizes crude geometry. Every layer reinforces Shared World crowds Chest Closed Standard, integrates with adjacent Zaylins systems, and passes recognition, lifecycle, town-style, accessibility, performance, and state review. Specialized GLBs remain outside the generic primitive Blender lane until a dedicated builder can satisfy this contract.

Match the district’s maintenance level rather than using uniform dirt or uniform perfection.

interactionAndAnimation.guidance: Separate parts that may open, rotate, light, display, receive an item, emit particles, take damage, change material, or connect to another system.
hooks: transform, material-state, damage, pickup, or placement hook only where gameplay requires it

productionBrief.collision: Use one or more primitive or low-complexity hulls matching the major blocking volume and interaction surface. Decorative handles, cables, slats, fasteners, trim, lenses, foliage, and surface detail must not create snagging collision.
productionBrief.orientationAndPivot: Use positive Z as the front or primary use direction and positive Y as up after export conversion. Place the origin at the ground contact, wall mount, suspension point, waterline, or logical placement center.
productionBrief.optimization: Preserve silhouette and interaction points, sharing repeated hardware and moving only microdetail into materials at lower LODs.

lod.lod0: Close-range output may use up to the reviewed maximum, with a practical target near 39,000 triangles when silhouette and required components justify it.
lod.lod1: Medium-range output should target roughly 18,000 triangles while preserving primary form, supports, interaction components, openings, material blocks, and essential lights.
lod.lod2: Far output should target roughly 6,000 triangles or a suitable impostor while retaining the recognizable outline, mounting or ground relationship, and major color or emissive signature.
lod.neverCollapse: The primary body and functional secondary parts must identify the object before labels or color. Handles, supports, openings, controls, edges, and contact points should explain use.

exportHierarchy: one named asset root
named render meshes grouped by functional component
separate animated or stateful parts
simplified collision objects or documented generated collision
material names tied to real construction categories
metadata for asset ID, town, family, source document, license, dimensions, and specification version
qaChecklist: Shared World crowds Feed In Braids Standard is recognizable from front, side, rear, and three-quarter views without relying only on text, decals, color, or glow.

The resolved semantic category is generic_prop because no stronger physical category was found, so the asset remains a generic prop; profession, species, customer, district, and narrative words do not override the physical object.
The result follows the shared-world art direction and does not borrow an unrelated town palette, technology level, weathering language, or decorative motif.
The overall envelope remains near 0.45 meters wide, 0.45 meters deep, and 0.45 meters high unless a reviewed override documents protruding hardware.
The asset has a coherent load path, support, mechanical system, anatomy, growth hierarchy, serving structure, or assembly logic appropriate to the resolved category.
Openings, access, supports, handles, controls, propulsion, joints, roots, containers, mounting, and contact points contain enough geometry to explain function.
Material boundaries follow real construction, growth, preparation, packaging, or manufacturing and do not act as arbitrary color blocking.
Transparent, flexible, organic, masonry, food, metal, wood, liquid, and emissive materials use believable thickness and response where present.
Placement, pivot, forward direction, scale, naming, hierarchy, and source metadata are export-ready.
Collision follows major blocking and interaction volumes without tracing decorative microdetail.
LOD plans preserve silhouette, support, interaction points, occupancy, openings, and the town-specific visual signature.
Four-angle previews contain no disconnected parts, accidental intersections, floating supports, inverted faces, open backs, hidden required components, or missing contact relationships.
The asset visibly supports the blueprint context “crowds hair” rather than acting as context-free filler.
The primary body and functional secondary parts must identify the object before labels or color. Handles, supports, openings, controls, edges, and contact points should explain use.

rejectionCriteria: generic primitive fallback for an unsupported family
humans assembled from cylinders and spheres without credible anatomy, clothing, hands, feet, face structure, and rigging
monsters or animals represented by stacked circles, repeated blobs, or disconnected primitive piles
vehicles without a readable chassis, passenger cabin, propulsion system, lighting, access panels, and stable stance
hover vehicles that are only a floating box or toy saucer
buildings that are only an undecorated rectangular shell when the specification requires a functional facade
one-material assets when the real object clearly contains distinct materials
unlabeled generic output quietly substituted for a requested asset
Roblox-like filler, toy-block proportions, or third-grade collage styling
random neon on assets whose town profile does not call for neon
generic primitive fallback or disconnected shape pile
toy-block proportions or Roblox-like filler
unexplained glow or random neon
missing origin, lifecycle, collision, state, service, or pooling metadata
visual noise that obscures gameplay readability
color-only communication without accessible alternatives
single undifferentiated material when separate layers are required
unlicensed copying of protected designs
reject a generic primitive substitute that omits the named object’s defining functional parts
reject one undifferentiated material when structural, flexible, transparent, emissive, organic, liquid, food, or service materials are visibly distinct
reject decorative complexity that does not explain use while handles, supports, openings, controls, fasteners, and contact points remain missing
